A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CAESAR/IDES research work. All pages are readable, including v1 Appendix A and v2 Appendices A–D; the text, equations, and algorithm displays support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical guarantees, proofs, and analytical MDP examples, but no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v2 adds algorithms and theoretical analyses, including policy identification, but neither the main text nor the appendices report original empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: v1 estimates target policies separately and constructs mixtures of their visitation distributions; using all deterministic policies is only suggested in Remark 4.1. v2 introduces MARCH, using an EULER-based policy cover and recursive importance weighting, and changes CAESAR to optimize over all deterministic policies. Algorithm 4 additionally introduces iterative policy elimination using CAESAR.

E1.justification: Neither version actually trains or evaluates on datasets or benchmarks. The all-deterministic-policy, policy-identification, and multi-reward extensions in v2 are theoretical settings, without executed evaluations.

E2.justification: Neither version reports evaluated experimental comparators. Comparisons with Dann et al. (2023), Yin and Wang (2020), and uniform sampling remain analytical. EULER becomes a method component, while the additional related-work citations do not establish new baseline evaluations.

E3.justification: Neither PDF reports experimental splits, evaluation metrics, model configurations, or testing protocols. Revised algorithmic sampling requirements concern the proposed methods and their theoretical guarantees, rather than experimental settings.

E4.justification: The analytical two-layer MDP examples and special-case calculations are retained. Neither version reports ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity experiments, or empirical case studies. The new appendix analyses develop formal guarantees.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run statistics, error bars, or significance tests. The Median-of-Means construction using O(log(1/delta)) independent estimators already appears in v1 Section 4.4 and is retained in v2 Section 4.4 and Appendix A.7.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries are reported in either version. The retained identical-policy, worst-case, and two-layer MDP examples preserve their analytical conclusions. New MARCH and policy-identification sample-complexity guarantees are formal additions assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Equations (5)–(6) enlarge the feasible sampling-distribution set. New Appendices B–C introduce beta-distance, supporting lemmas and proofs, and Theorem B.2 claiming polynomial sample dependence for coarse estimation of all deterministic policies. Appendix D adds the policy-identification guarantee and proof. Existing SGD and main-theorem arguments are largely relocated to Appendices A.5 and A.7.

C1.justification: v2 Section 3.1 adds MARCH as an independent contribution and claims polynomial sample dependence despite an exponentially large deterministic-policy class, addressing a possibility left unresolved in v1 Remark 4.1. CAESAR's optimal-sampling claim now covers mixtures over all deterministic policies, although the displayed leading sample-complexity formula retains its form.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly characterizes the lower-bound comparison as variance-unaware and proposes variance-aware analysis as future work. Section 5.3 and Appendix D add interpretations connecting near-optimal policy sets to action-value gaps and explaining multi-reward difficulty through policy similarity. Existing discussions of overlap, horizon dependence, and sparse rewards remain.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly initializes IDES through a dummy initial state and transition P0 equal to the initial-state distribution, replacing v1's empty-distribution shorthand. Appendix B supplies MARCH tolerances and the 2HSA importance-weight clipping level. The IDES projection bound was already documented in v1 Appendix A.5; neither version supplies code or hardware information.

R1.justification: v2 adds a substantive paragraph comparing its objectives and ratio estimation with concurrent work by Amortila et al. (2024). It also adds Jin et al. (2020), Dann et al. (2021), and Simchowitz and Jamieson (2019) to support the new exploration and policy-identification material. Most existing research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: The main text receives extensive language editing and a new historical Caesar opening. The former Section 4.5 discussion becomes a separate section with subsections, while the SGD lemma and main-theorem derivation move from the main text into Appendix A. These changes substantially reorganize the narrative beyond merely adding scientific content.

P2.justification: v2 reformats the manuscript throughout with a narrower text block, restyled title and references, and reflowed equations and algorithm boxes. IDES and CAESAR displays are relocated, and Algorithms 3–4 add two new pseudocode displays. Neither version contains experimental plots or result tables.

improvement.justification: v2 offers a potentially important resolution of v1's all-deterministic-policy sampling limitation, adds policy-identification theory, and improves organization. However, new Algorithm 3 omits the policy-action factor appearing in its proof, and Lemma B.4's first inequality fails under Definition B.1: x=1, y=0, beta=1, epsilon=1/2 satisfies the distance premise but yields the false bound 1 <= 3/4. These newly introduced inconsistencies leave support for the central extension uncertain, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
